# Compliance review — ABP Final Report (draft)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Customer** | Associated British Ports (ABP) |
| **Document reviewed** | ABP Report .pdf — 51 PDF pages, exported 15 October 2026 |
| **Template** | `report/final_report_template_v1.md` |
| **Review date** | 15 October 2026 |
| **Page numbering** | No page prints a number. Cited pages are the document's own (Word) numbers = PDF − 1, confirmed against every TOC entry from §1 (p. 4) to 4.1 (p. 18). From 4.2 onwards the TOC is stale (H3) |
| **Section numbering** | The report numbers its sections one lower than the template (report §1 Executive Summary = template §2). This review uses the report's numbers |
| **Verdict** | **Not ready for peer review** — 9 blocking issues: the ROI is below the band, contradicted in §4, and rests on an incomplete, unvalidated cost and benefit base; the PoV is unsized and has no deliverables or success criteria tables |

## Summary

The draft explains a hard scheduling problem clearly and keeps people in charge of every consequential decision (pp. 5, 14, 21). Five value drivers are derived in full and reconcile to the P&L to the pound (pp. 18, 30–33). The infrastructure sizing is specific and argued (p. 48). The six survey use cases each get a careful detail sheet (pp. 34–42).

Nine issues block peer review. The ROI is 83%, below the 100% floor (B1), and §4 opens by calling it 38% (B2). There are no recurring costs (B3) and nothing is validated by ABP (B4). The PoV has no day size or commercial basis (B5), no deliverables table (B6) and no success criteria (B7), and runs on synthetic data, which needs an agreed exception (B8). There is no vendor appendix (B9).

## Blocking issues

### B1 — The ROI is 83%, below the 100% floor, with no ramp and with the PoV and running costs left out

**Rule.** The first use case lands between 100% and 300%. Below 100%: do not inflate; revisit the scope, check for omitted benefits, escalate to the engagement lead, and report the honest figure. Year 1 benefit is ramped at about 50%.

**Evidence.** The P&L ties: £1,214,040 benefit, £662,993 cost, £551,047 net, 83% (p. 18). The draft calls the case "conservative" (pp. 5, 18, 30), but "No ramp-up is applied in this conservative steady-state table" (p. 19), the £60,000 PoV is excluded (F3), and there are no running costs (B3).

On the report's own figures: including the PoV gives 68%; a 50% Year 1 ramp gives 65% (net £429,643); both give 51% [my calculations]. B3 lowers it further.

**Fix.** Escalate to Mike before peer review. Legitimate routes, none of which raises a rate:
- Omitted benefit. Overtime is listed as "Not monetised - overtime baseline required" (p. 33). Add it as a sixth driver: `[NEEDS INPUT: annual pilot and marine overtime spend at the main hubs, from ABP Finance]`.
- Scope. Cisco hardware for three regions is £356,193, 54% of total cost, while the PoV and Foundation stage centre on one hub (pp. 5, 22, 24). Test a one-region first production step: `[NEEDS INPUT: Cisco pricing for a single-region start]`.
- If it stays under 100%, report it as such, apply the ramp, and drop "conservative" from pp. 5, 18 and 30.

### B2 — §4 opens with an ROI of 38%; everywhere else it is 83%

**Rule.** The headline figure is identical wherever it appears.

**Evidence.** "the five-year model indicates an estimated net benefit of approximately £551k and an ROI of around 38%" (p. 17). The same net benefit gives 83% on pp. 5 and 18.

**Fix.** Replace "around 38%" with the figure agreed under B1. Search the source document for any other stale figure.

### B3 — The cost base has no running costs

**Rule.** Full five-year recurring and support costs; client-side effort included; the P&L's OPEX block names each licence.

**Evidence.** Every cost sits in Year 1; Years 2–5 are "-" (p. 18). There is no 3AIgent licence line. The configuration includes "the associated Cisco and NVIDIA subscriptions" (p. 48), but their term is not stated. Note 2 reads: "Production infrastructure, implementation, integration and recurring platform costs are TBC" (p. 18), although the first three are itemised in the same table. There is no ABP effort line, although §1.3 and §6.3 ask for operational representatives, data and rule review (pp. 6, 25).

**Fix.** Add the OPEX block: `[NEEDS INPUT: 3AIgent annual licence, from Phill]`, `[NEEDS INPUT: Cisco and NVIDIA subscription term and Years 2–5 support, from the Cisco account team]`, `[NEEDS INPUT: ABP days for planners, rule owners, IT and training]`. Rewrite note 2 to name only what is still open. Re-run B1.

### B4 — Only the pilot count is ABP's; the other inputs are 3Point assumptions, and nothing is signed off

**Rule.** Every figure and assumption is confirmed by named ABP staff with dates, in the appendix "ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off". Drivers rest on customer denominators.

**Evidence.** The arithmetic is shown and correct (pp. 30–33). The customer data: 160 pilots "based on the workshop notes" (p. 19) and the 45–60 minute waiting range (p. 32). Not ABP's:
- 100 assignments per pilot (p. 19): no source. Every driver multiplies from it.
- £75 per launch trip: "not an official benchmark and should be replaced with ABP actual cost data" (p. 30). The 20% groupable share (p. 30) and the 30% taxi share and £16.50 fare (p. 30) are unsourced.
- Salaries are Skills England medians, not ABP pay (p. 19).
- Benefit 5: £5,500 a day "Indicative benchmark", 12 hours "Illustrative", and 10 missed tides with no source (pp. 19, 33). A vessel's operating cost normally falls on the shipowner, not ABP [inferred]; the driver needs to show ABP's own loss.

Note 1 calls the figures "indicative rather than an ABP-approved P&L commitment" (p. 18). The sign-off appendix and both validation statements are absent (pp. 30–50 searched).

**Fix.** `[NEEDS INPUT: annual assignments per hub, launch trips and marginal launch cost, taxi journeys and spend, missed-tide events in the last year and ABP's cost per event — from ABP Marine Operations and Finance]`. Add the appendix with one row per input and cost line, marked outstanding until confirmed.

### B5 — The PoV is "one month" and £60,000 in the P&L; there is no day size, payer or environment

**Rule.** §7.1 (here §6) states effort (20 or 40 days), elapsed duration, team, commercial basis and environment; the summary and conclusion repeat the day size. Size and scope are agreed with Phill before peer review.

**Evidence.** The four-week plan is clear, week by week (p. 24), and scope and exclusions are specific (pp. 5–6, 15). "Proof of Value £60,000" appears only as a P&L column (p. 18). No page gives days, the team beyond "3Point will lead" (p. 25), who pays, or where the demonstration runs.

**Fix.** Add the "PoV at a glance" table to §6 and an effort profile summing to the size; the four weekly rows on p. 24 map onto workstreams. Commercial basis in the template's neutral wording: `[NEEDS INPUT: size in days, price and commercial basis as agreed with Phill; PoV environment]`.

### B6 — PoV outputs are well listed but there is no deliverables table

**Rule.** Mandatory in §7.1: receivable artefacts, each with a format and named recipient, each backed by days, ending with the PoV outcome report and production recommendation.

**Evidence.** The weekly "Expected deliverables" column (p. 24) and the six "expected outputs" (p. 28) are good material. None has a format, recipient or days.

**Fix.** Insert after the p. 24 table:

| # | Deliverable | Format | Received and accepted by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agreed PoV scope: hub, scenarios, rule subset, dataset | Document | `[NEEDS INPUT: ABP operational lead]` |
| 2 | Planning demonstration: assignment, duty/rest, shared transport, disruption, approval | Working software in `[NEEDS INPUT: environment]` | `[NEEDS INPUT: lead marine information officer]` |
| 3 | Pilot mobile journeys: assignments, alerts, acknowledgements, status | Working software | `[NEEDS INPUT: pilot representative]` |
| 4 | PAVIS integration options assessment | Document | `[NEEDS INPUT: ABP IT owner of PAVIS]` |
| 5 | PoV outcome report and production recommendation, with implementation scope and roadmap | Document and readout | `[NEEDS INPUT: sponsor]` |

### B7 — Acceptance criteria are deferred; there is no success criteria table

**Rule.** Mandatory in §7.1: each criterion has a measure and data source, a baseline, a target and a linked KPI or value driver; agreed with a named ABP role before the PoV starts; at least one business-outcome and one user-acceptance measure.

**Evidence.** Agreeing criteria is itself an action: "Agree demonstration acceptance criteria" (pp. 6, 28). §6.5 names the review subjects — planner experience, clarity of pilot communications, exception handling (p. 26). The workshop KPIs exist: taxi spend, launch usage "1% increase is good enough", waiting time 45–60 minutes (p. 50).

**Fix.** Add the table to §6:

| # | Criterion | Measure and source | Baseline | Target | Linked driver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fewer launch movements | Vessels per launch on the replayed scenarios (B8) | `[NEEDS INPUT]` | +1% (p. 50) or `[NEEDS INPUT]` | Benefit 1 |
| 2 | Lower taxi use | Taxi journeys per 100 assignments, same scenarios | `[NEEDS INPUT]` | `[NEEDS INPUT]` | Benefit 2 |
| 3 | Mandatory rules applied | Share of proposed plans passing every configured rest and certification check | — | 100% | KPI catalogue |
| 4 | Planner acceptance | Marine information officers rating plans usable without rework | — | `[NEEDS INPUT]` | Benefit 3 |

Add "Success criteria agreed by: `[NEEDS INPUT: name, role, date]`".

### B8 — The PoV is a demonstration on synthetic data that will not test the value case

**Rule.** The PoV proves the value hypothesis "on the customer's own data".

**Evidence.** A deliberate and openly stated choice: "representative sample or synthetic data … rather than a complete operational solution" (p. 5); the PoV "will not establish production readiness, validate live PAVIS integration or substantiate financial savings" (p. 29).

**Fix.** Either record an agreed exception with Phill and Mike, with one sentence of reason (`[NEEDS INPUT: why ABP data is not available for the PoV]`), or replay one historical week of the chosen hub's real assignments through the planner, which measures B7 rows 1–2 against what actually happened `[NEEDS INPUT: ABP agreement to share one week of hub data]`. This is the third consecutive draft with a simulated PoV (SSC-ICT, DVZ-MV); the template probably needs a "simulated demonstration" variant.

### B9 — No vendor appendix

**Rule.** "Vendors and Third-Party Components" is a mandatory appendix.

**Evidence.** Absent from the TOC (pp. 1–3) and from pp. 30–50.

**Fix.** Add the appendix from the sweep table at the end of this review and complete the three procurement notes.

## Section-by-section findings

**§1 Executive Summary (pp. 4–7).** F11: about three pages, with the business case figures (p. 5) and a PoV-first recommendation. Missing: thank-you (X1), the at-a-glance table, the pillars table, the day size (B5), and a next-steps table; the six numbered priorities (p. 6) have no owner, timeframe or ROI sign-off row.

**§2 Current State and Strategic Drives (pp. 7–10).** F13: six challenges and six objectives, each clearly argued in business terms. Neither the challenges table nor the objectives mapping table is present. Four pages against two.

**§3.1 Use Case Identification (p. 11).** F6: "a wider set of suggested AI opportunities". Appendix 8.2 says "six opportunities submitted through the ABP AI Use Case Survey" (p. 34). Fix: "ABP colleagues submitted 6 candidate use cases `[NEEDS INPUT: contributor count and functions, from the 3AIm export]`; two were combined into the selected opportunity." Add the funnel and a six-row portfolio table.

**§3.2 Selected Priority Use Cases (pp. 11–16).** F14: the three functional areas (p. 11), the business problem (p. 12) and the eleven-row features table with PoV treatment (pp. 15–16) are exactly right. The decision boundary is explicit: AI functions "would not independently determine certification, relax rest requirements or authorise operational changes" (p. 14). Missing: the four-way benefits (the three value categories on p. 17 hold the material), the interfaces table (desktop and mobile are described on pp. 9, 13), and the solution design table. The seven-step workflow the template asks for is on p. 44.

**§4 Financial Case (pp. 17–19).** B1–B4, F1–F5.
- **F1.** The P&L is a pasted Windows metafile object (`Meta189`, p. 18), not a native table. It has a PoV column, no CAPEX/OPEX block or total rows, and six notes in place of the three standing ones; VAT and expenses are not mentioned.
- **F2.** Cumulative net benefit is −£420,185, −£177,377, then +£65,431 [my calculation]: payback in Year 3. Add the row and the sentence.
- **F4.** No conservative/expected/optimistic table. P&L "Released marine planning capacity" is "Released marine planning and coordination capacity" in the appendix (p. 31); "Avoided vessel missing a tide slot" is "Reduced vessel delay risk" on p. 17; Benefit 4's names also differ. The excluded-benefits table (p. 33) is good and stays.
- **F5.** The p. 19 graphic gives £163k and £79k a year, £1,214k over five years, all of which reconcile to the P&L [checked]. Rebuild it as the native risk table with "value forgone" wording.

**§5 Target AI Platform (pp. 20–23).** X3, X8, F8–F10. Five architecture principles are tied to the solution (p. 21), and the System of Record's coexistence with PAVIS is handled carefully (p. 21). # Final Report Compliance Review — American University of Beirut

|---|---|
| **Customer** | American University of Beirut (AUB) |

| **Overall verdict** | **Not ready for peer review** — 7 blocking issues |

## Summary

A well-argued draft with a strong technical core. The end-to-end interaction flow (pp. 11–14) is the clearest articulation of a grounded, deterministic-rules-plus-LLM design I have reviewed against this template, and keeping eligibility decisions out of the LLM is right and well explained. Seven issues block peer review: the figures are promised for later validation rather than customer-confirmed; the six value drivers carry benchmark rates with no AUB denominator; the POV is sized at 26–32 person-days against the 20/40-day rule and never priced; its deliverables and success criteria carry neither required column set; Section 5.1 is a pasted spreadsheet object with no narrative; and the vendors appendix is absent.

## Blocking issues

### B1 — Financial figures are promised for later validation, not confirmed by named AUB staff (p. 29)

The report states the opposite of the template's position. Page 29: "Financial assumptions should be validated during the pilot using AUB-specific advising, registration, and retention data." Page 28 lists "Validate business benefits and complete the production ROI model" as the last immediate action, after "Conduct the controlled Proof of Value".

Every ROI figure and assumption must be confirmed as accurate by named AUB staff, with dates, in the appendix "ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off", before submission. That appendix does not exist — the appendix run is 8.1 to 8.7 (pp. 2–3, 28–39) with no equivalent item — and no name or date appears against any figure anywhere in the document.

**Action.** Hold a validation session, record each material figure with the AUB name, role and date that confirmed it, and add the appendix.

### B2 — Six value drivers carry benchmark rates but no AUB denominator (pp. 15, 38–39)

The driver structure is good and the benchmark discipline is better than most: each of the six drivers on p. 15 is tied on pp. 38–39 to a named source with a stated range and the conservative rate actually applied — "1.0% to 2.0% increase in overall student retention… applies a conservative 0.25% to 0.85%", "40% to 75% containment rates… conservatively assumes a 20% (Year 1) to 36% (Year 4) query deflection". That is the right instinct and should survive.

Missing is the AUB half of every calculation. There is no tuition fee, no current attrition rate, no advisor headcount or salary, no annual enquiry volume, no temp-staff or overtime spend. Without them there is no path from "0.25% to 0.85% retention gain" to USD 3,600,000 of preventable tuition loss, and a CFO cannot check USD 8,650,000. The engagement holds part of the base — 7,000–8,000 undergraduates and ~1,500 courses (pp. 3, 30) — so the denominators are likely obtainable. Two drivers need a stated basis rather than a rate: "Deferred Incremental Advisor Capacity" rests on deferring two advisor hires with no salary given, and "Shared AI Platform Multi-Use Cost Avoidance" (USD 1,200,000) rests on future use cases that are costed nowhere (F7).

**Action.** For each driver, state the AUB base quantity, the rate applied and the resulting figure, in the appendix "Detailed Financial Models".

### B3 — The POV is sized at 26–32 person-days against the 20/40-day rule and is never priced (pp. 18, 22)

The sizing work is done and stated candidly. Page 22: "Approximately 26-32 person-days, delivered over an elapsed period of approximately 20 working days through parallel execution", with a role-by-role table on p. 22 that sums correctly to that range, and the honest qualifier "Not every role is required full-time throughout the POV." This is a disclosed deviation, not an oversight.

It still breaches two rules. The effort table must sum to the stated size, and the size is 20 days or 40 days — 26–32 is neither, and 20 working days is elapsed duration, not effort. Separately, no commercial basis appears anywhere in Section 7: no price, and no statement of whether this is a firm price, jointly funded, or subject to a Cisco funding discussion. The only price in the document is "Proof of Value - student advisor 30,600" inside the P&L on p. 15, never referenced from Section 7 and not divisible into either day count. The report correctly makes no claim that Cisco is funding it.

**Action.** Agree the size with Phill — re-cut to 20 days, or carry 40 with the reason stated — then put it, the commercial basis and the price in Sections 2.2, 2.3, 7.1 and the conclusion, and make the effort table sum to it.

### B4 — POV deliverables are a twelve-item list with no format, recipient or day backing (p. 23)

The list is real work product rather than activities: "Ellucian Banner integration prototype", "Source-grounded AI responses with citations", "Production infrastructure sizing recommendation", and it correctly closes with "POV findings and next-phase roadmap" — the artefact the go/no-go decision rests on.

It is not the mandatory table. No deliverable carries a format, none carries a named AUB recipient who accepts it, and none maps to days in the p. 22 role table — the "Deliverables" column of the p. 20–21 work plan is a different, ten-item set that does not reconcile with these twelve. Twelve is also double the template's 4–6, and several entries ("Configured LLM and RAG environment on Cisco AI POD", "Security and guardrail configuration") are environment states rather than things AUB can take away.

**Action.** Rebuild as the Section 7.1 table with 4–6 rows, each a receivable artefact with a format and a named AUB role, each backed by days in the effort profile.

### B5 — POV success criteria are qualitative and their thresholds are deferred to discovery (p. 24)

The seven "POV Acceptance Criteria" bullets on p. 24 are well chosen and cover the right risks, including the two that matter most here: "Course eligibility/prerequisite decisions use deterministic academic logic rather than being generated by the LLM" and "Unauthorized student information is not exposed."

None is measurable as written. There is no baseline, no target, no data source and no linked KPI or value driver on any of the seven, and p. 24 states plainly: "Quantitative accuracy and performance thresholds will be agreed during the initial discovery phase and measured during the POV." That is the retrospective position the template forbids. No named AUB role and no date is recorded as having agreed them.

The targets exist. They are on p. 13 in the "Proposed Target for KPIs" table — >95% accuracy on a validated advising test set, ~100% grounded answers, 100% deterministic eligibility decisions, <5 sec latency, <5–10% unanswered queries. This is a consolidation problem, not a creation problem. Note that p. 13 carries no baseline and no business-outcome or user-acceptance measure, so it cannot be lifted across unchanged.

**Action.** Move the p. 13 targets into a Section 7.1 success criteria table, add a baseline and data source to each, add one business outcome and one user acceptance criterion, and record the AUB role and date that agreed them before the POV starts.

### B6 — Section 5.1 is a pasted spreadsheet object with no narrative, assumptions or payback statement (p. 15)

The model underneath is sound. Recomputed independently, every row ties: the six benefit rows sum to 720,000 / 1,750,000 / 2,680,000 / 3,500,000 by year and 8,650,000 in total; costs sum to 2,430,223; Net Benefit equals Total Benefits less Total Cost in every year; cumulative net benefit turns positive in Year 2, matching the "Within Year 2" payback on p. 3; and 6,219,777 / 2,430,223 = 256%. Charging the entire USD 1,720,240 Cisco platform to the first use case is conservative and is a large part of why the figure lands inside the guardrail.

The presentation breaches the house format. The table is an embedded object — a Form XObject carrying its own font resources, including an Aptos Display face used nowhere else in the document — not a native table, so it cannot be edited by a reviewer and extracts out of reading order. Section 5.1 contains nothing else: no narrative, no value realisation principles, no assumptions block, no benefit realisation percentage, no ramp assumption, no client-side effort in the investment, no payback paragraph, and none of the three standing notes verbatim (p. 15 substitutes five notes of its own). The section runs to one page against a three-page budget.

**Action.** Rebuild the P&L as a native 10pt table in the four-block house format with the three standing notes verbatim, and write the narrative, assumptions and payback paragraph around it.

### B7 — No vendors appendix; NVIDIA, Red Hat, the vector database and the LLM sit outside the costed lines (pp. 15, 20, 33–35)

Mandatory appendix, absent — the run is 8.1 to 8.7 with no equivalent item. The full sweep is the last section of this review.

The commercial risk is concrete. Page 15 carries "Cisco AI Platform Capex 1,720,240" and "Cisco Hardware and Software installation 40,000" and nothing states what is inside them. Four NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs (p. 35) are presumably included but not itemised. Red Hat is never named although "Kubernetes / OpenShift" appears seven times and OpenShift is a licensed subscription. The vector database is named only by category on pp. 17, 19–20 and 35 while being an explicit line in both the POV and production configurations. The LLM is specified only as "8B–14B class" with no provider. And the P&L line "Cisco AI Platform Opex, subscriptions, upgrades and support" is costed at zero across all five columns (F5), so four years of support on a USD 1.72m platform is carried at nothing.

**Action.** Add the appendix with a commercial status against every vendor, name the vector database and the model provider or state that the choice is open, and confirm in the p. 15 cost breakdown what the two Cisco lines contain.

## Section-by-section findings

**Section 1 — Table of Contents.** Two pages against one (pp. 1–2), inflated by the 8.X appendix entries at F1 and by three levels of numbering. Page references are accurate: all 38 entries were checked against measured heading positions and every one landed correctly — unusual, and worth saying given H2.

**Section 2 — Executive Summary.** Three pages, inside budget (pp. 3–5), and the opening framing is in student and advisor terms rather than technology terms. F2: 256% appears exactly twice in the document, on p. 3 and p. 15, against the four places the template requires — it is in neither 2.1 nor the conclusion. Page 3 also labels it "Return on Investment (ROI) 5 Years" while p. 15 reads "ROI over 4 years"; the model runs an implementation year plus four benefit years, so the p. 3 label is wrong. F10: 2.1 argues the case well in five value levers (p. 4) but carries no strategic pillars table and no figure of any kind. F8: 2.2 (p. 5) promises three stages — PoV, Controlled Pilot, Production and Expansion — but 7.4 (pp. 24–26) goes straight from POV to a twelve-phase production build, so Stage 2 has no duration, owner or cost anywhere.

**Section 3 — Current State and Strategic Drivers.** ✅ Content conforms (pp. 6–7) and sits inside its two-page budget. The eight challenges are correctly framed as structural business problems rather than IT gaps, and urgency is kept qualitative as the template asks. F11 is a formatting finding only: they are bold prose headings where the template specifies a table with urgency and cost-of-inaction columns, and 3.2 (pp. 7–8) lists ten objectives with no mapping to supporting use cases.

**Section 4 — Prioritised AI Opportunities.** Seven pages against four (pp. 8–14), the largest contributor to X3. F3: the count is stated — "38 potential AI use cases" (p. 8) — which is the thing most drafts get wrong, and the funnel narrows credibly to five and then one with the selection reasoning given on p. 11. But the 38-row table itself occupies pp. 9–11 of the body where the template puts the long list in the appendix "Use Case Detail Sheets"; contributor and function breadth are not given; the five-row funnel table is absent; and no submission carries an outcome. F9: the portfolio table has only a short description per row, with no business priority, headline impact or status column, and only the pilot has a detail sheet (pp. 29–31) against five shortlisted use cases. 4.2's heading is singular where the template is plural. The interaction flow at 4.2.2 (pp. 11–14) is the strongest content in the report.

**Section 5 — Financial Case.** One page against three (p. 15) — the only section under budget, and that is a symptom of B6, not economy. F12: 5.2's seven risks (pp. 15–16) are well chosen and correctly framed as value forgone, but carry no quantified annual cost of inaction, although the p. 15 P&L drivers are precisely their inverse. The numbers are one page away.

**Section 6 — Target AI Platform.** ✅ Two pages, on budget (pp. 16–17), and 6.1's reuse argument is well made — the reusable services are named individually, four growth phases are set out, and the point that advising capacity can scale during registration without scaling other services is exactly the right one. Cisco positioning is at X2.

**Section 7 — Implementation Roadmap.** Nine pages against three (pp. 18–26), the second contributor to X3. The work plan (pp. 20–21), project resources (p. 22), client resources (p. 23) and delivery team (pp. 25–26) are good content in the wrong place: all of it belongs in the appendix "POV Scope and Work Breakdown", which does not exist. F6: no explicit out-of-scope list appears anywhere in 7.1–7.4. The closest thing is "Banner integration should initially be read-only" on p. 33 — in an appendix, and about the solution rather than the POV. The fifteen-item POV inclusion list on p. 18 reads as the full end-to-end solution, so nothing in the document holds the day estimate. The unnumbered headings "Work Plan", "Project Resources", "Recommended Delivery Team" and "Required AUB Resources" sit at three different sizes (16pt, 14pt, 13.5pt) and appear in the TOC alongside numbered entries.

**Conclusion and Next Steps.** F1: the heading carries no section number and its subsections run 7.5, 7.6 and 7.7 (pp. 27–28), so the document has eight top-level sections where the template has nine. F13: 7.6 is a twelve-item bullet list with no owner and no deadline, and the fixed first row — customer confirmation of the ROI figures — appears last, after "Conduct the controlled Proof of Value", inverting the release-control sequence. 7.7 gives three dimensions rather than the 6-month / 12-month / 3–5-year horizons and carries no figure from Section 5.1. Twelve recommendations against the template's 3–5, though recommendation 1 is correctly the POV.

**Appendices.** F1: numbered 8.1–8.7 with TOC entries, against the rule that appendix items are plain labels with neither. F4: 8.1 "Detailed Financial Models" (pp. 28–29) specifies a model to be built — "The detailed financial model should evaluate…", "The model should include", twelve bullets — rather than presenting one. There is no year-by-year table, no per-driver derivation, no sensitivity analysis and no per-use-case P&L, so the six driver names in the p. 15 P&L have nothing to reconcile to. This is where B2's derivations must go. F14: 8.5 (p. 36) is a change assessment only — no stakeholder matrix, no skills assessment, no resistance assessment, no training plan, despite the heading naming stakeholders. F15: 8.6 (p. 37) lists 27 KPI names across five groups with no definition, baseline, target, frequency, data source or owner; the p. 13 table already has targets for nine of them. F16: 8.7 (pp. 38–39) is the best-argued appendix in the report and names Gartner, McKinsey, Deloitte, IDC, Cisco and Ellucian with the ranges actually applied, but gives no publication title, no date and no report-section mapping, so none of it is traceable. 8.3 (pp. 31–33) and 8.4 (pp. 32–35) conform in substance; the design principles on p. 33 and the GPU selection rationale on p. 34 are strong. Three mandatory appendices are absent: ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off, POV Scope and Work Breakdown, and Vendors and Third-Party Components.

## Cross-cutting findings

### X1 — Drafted against the older 3Point template (throughout)

No `[!MANDATORY]` or `[!HIGHLIGHT]` callout content appears anywhere — not the opening thank-you, not the ROI validation statement, not the POV recommendation, not the closing "Following the conclusion of our engagement together" formula. The hierarchy is `3Point_Final_Client_Report_Template.md`, not v1: its appendix labels match verbatim, including the lower-cased "Infra sizing", "Stakeholder and change assessment" and "Analyst sources and benchmark", and its numbering survives in the dangling "Refer to Appendix 9.6" on p. 28 (E5).

This single fact explains B4, B5, B7, F1, F3, F10, F11 and F13 together. Re-basing the draft on v1 resolves most of them mechanically and is faster than fixing them one at a time.

### X2 — The Cisco Secure AI Factory is never named, and the platform economics are never quantified (pp. 16–18)

The phrase "Cisco Secure AI Factory" does not appear. Cisco is present throughout as infrastructure — the AI POD, UCS C845A M8, Intersight, AI Defense, Hypershield, Isovalent — and 6.1 makes the platform argument properly: the assistant is framed as "the first production use case of a broader University AI Platform, rather than a standalone chatbot", the reusable services are named, and four growth phases are set out (pp. 17–18). The naming is the gap, not the argument.

Quantification is the real absence. There is no Section 6.1 economics table and neither required economic is stated in figures. The numbers exist elsewhere: p. 38 gives IDC's "30% to 50%" reduction in the marginal deployment cost of subsequent use cases, and p. 15 carries "Shared AI Platform Multi-Use Cost Avoidance" at USD 1,200,000. Both belong in 6.1, split into one-time foundation cost against per-use-case delivery cost, with the comparison basis footnoted.

**Action.** Name the platform in Sections 2 and 6, and add the 6.1 economics table drawing on the p. 15 and p. 38 figures.

### X3 — Main body 28 pages against ~20 (pp. 1–28)

Measured from the TOC page references. Sections 4 and 7 account for the entire overrun; Sections 2, 3, 6 and the conclusion are on budget and Section 5 is under it.

| Section | Pages | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Table of Contents | 1–2 | 1 |
| 2. Executive Summary | 3–5 | 3 |
| 3. Current State | 6–7 | 2 |
| 4. Prioritised AI Opportunities | 8–14 | 4 |
| 5. Financial Case | 15 | 3 |
| 6. Target AI Platform | 16–17 | 2 |
| 7. Implementation Roadmap | 18–26 | 3 |
| 8. Conclusion (unnumbered) | 27–28 | 2 |
| **Main body** | **~28** | **~20** |

**Action.** Move the 38-row long list (pp. 9–11) to "Use Case Detail Sheets" and the work plan, project resources, client resources and delivery team (pp. 20–26) to "POV Scope and Work Breakdown", leaving cross-references. That recovers about eight pages and creates two of the three missing appendices.

### X4 — Only Sections 2 and 5 start at the top of a page (pp. 6, 8, 16, 18, 27, 28)

Section 2 begins at the top of p. 3 and Section 5 at the top of p. 15. Every other numbered section begins part-way down a page carrying the previous section's text: Section 3 below the 2.3 narrative on p. 6, Section 4 below the 3.2 bullets on p. 8, Section 6 halfway down p. 16, Section 7 in the bottom third of p. 18, the Conclusion below the delivery-team table on p. 27, and Section 8 near the foot of p. 28 with "8.1 Detailed Financial Models" immediately beneath it — a heading pair stranded at the page foot. Among appendix items, only 8.5 (p. 36) and 8.6 (p. 37) start a new page; 8.7 is stranded at the foot of p. 37. There are no stray blank pages, so no simulated breaks are present — the breaks were simply never applied.

**Action.** Set "page break before" and "keep with next" on the Heading 1 style and on the appendix item style, then regenerate the TOC.

## House style and typography

Measured from embedded font resources and text-rendering operators. The core is right: body text is Aptos 12pt throughout and heading levels are consistent at 20pt and 16pt. The drift is at the edges, where the template says it survives review.

| ID | Element | Found | House style |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Running header, all 38 pages | Times New Roman 10pt, ~2,850 characters | Aptos 9pt |
| H2 | Page numbers | None rendered on any page | Aptos 9pt |
| H3 | Cover title / headings | Aptos 22pt / Aptos 20pt and 16pt | Aptos Display 28pt bold / 20pt and 16pt bold |
| H4 | Table body | 11pt (pp. 9–10, 25–26), 12pt (pp. 13–14) | Aptos 10pt |
| H5 | Figure captions | Aptos italic 10pt | Aptos 9pt italic |
| H6 | Front matter | No generation date, version or review_status on the cover | all three required |

H1 is the cleanest single fix in the document: one header style, on every page, in the wrong face. H2 and H5 compound each other — the TOC page references are accurate but the pages carry no numbers, so a reader cannot use them. Eight figures are numbered and captioned, which is better than most drafts, but none is referenced by number from the narrative, the image on p. 36 is uncaptioned and unnumbered, and no table anywhere in the document is captioned or numbered.

Two notes on evidence. The p. 15 P&L being an embedded object is verified, not inferred: it is a Form XObject with its own font resources (B6). ArialMT is declared in the font resources of thirty pages, but every run set in it that I could find carries only whitespace — it looks like a latent Word theme font rather than actual drift. Worth a glance in the source .docx; not a finding on this evidence.

## Editorial defects

| ID | Page | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 15 | "Total Amercan University of Beyrouth Systems ROI over 4 years" — two misspellings in the P&L title row | Correct both to "American University of Beirut" |
| E2 | 15 | Cost line "AI Solution Implementation 3Point - AI-Powered Ticket Consolidation USD 315,333" — another engagement's use case in a client-facing table | Rename to the AUB scope |
| E3 | cover, 3, 15, 27 | "AUoB" on the cover, in the first line of the summary, in the P&L and at "AUoB should:"; "AUB" everywhere else | Pick one form and apply it throughout |
| E4 | 1, 6 | "Current State and Strategic Drives" | "Drivers" — correct in heading and TOC |
| E5 | 28 | "Refer to Appendix 9.6 for the complete KPI catalogue" — no 9.6 exists | Reference the KPI catalogue by name |
| E6 | cover, 8 | "During the the AI Realisation Workshop"; the cover reads "AI Readiness Assessment" | Fix the duplicate; confirm which workshop name is house standard |
| E7 | 3, 8, 11, 34, 38 | "personalized", "prioritized", "analyzes", "optimize", "enrollment", "Centralizing" beside "programme", "organisational", "prioritised" | Set the language to en-GB and run a spelling pass |
| E8 | 23 | Key deliverable "13." is blank | Delete or complete |
| E9 | 9–10 | Raw submission titles in a client-facing table — "I Didn't Get the Question / Submission does not define a specific AI use case", "The First Idea", "No I Work in Nursing", "a101" | Retitle, or move the list to the appendix with an outcome per row |
| E10 | 3, 33 | "Nexus" refers to both AUB Nexus (Ellucian Experience) and Cisco Nexus | Qualify each on first use |
| E11 | cover | PDF metadata author "Lourdes Ruiz and Alberto Pollieri"; cover byline "Amir Ashour & Eric Mitha" | Correct document properties before issue |

## What is working well

- The end-to-end interaction flow (pp. 11–14) is the best content in the report: six numbered steps, an explicit separation of institutional knowledge from student data, and the plain statement that "The LLM therefore does not independently decide whether a student is eligible for a course."
- The P&L arithmetic ties on every row and the 256% ROI sits inside the 100–300% guardrail without needing a haircut — partly because the whole USD 1,720,240 platform cost is charged to the first use case, which is the conservative choice and should survive review.
- The long list is counted, not waved at: 38 candidates, narrowed to five, narrowed to one, with the selection reasoning stated on p. 11.
- The analyst appendix (pp. 38–39) states both the benchmark range and the more conservative rate actually applied for each of the six drivers — the discipline the template asks for, and rarely delivered.
- The GPU choice is argued rather than asserted (p. 34): RTX PRO 6000 over an H200 configuration on workload grounds, with "A 70B-class model should not be considered an initial requirement" stated plainly.
- Sizing assumptions are labelled honestly — "These are sizing assumptions to validate during POV, not facts collected in the workshop" (p. 34).

## Method and limitations

- Text, embedded fonts, per-page image inventory and text-rendering operators extracted with `pypdf` 6.14.2. Poppler is not installed, so pages were not rendered.
- I cannot see images. Figures 1–8 (pp. 11, 16, 17, 18, 25, 31, 32, 35) and the uncaptioned image on p. 36 were not read; I have not inferred their content. Figures 2, 6 and 7 are architecture and sizing diagrams and very likely carry vendor names I could not extract — the sweep below is text-only and will be short of them.
- Printed page numbers are cited throughout, offset one below PDF page numbers (cover unnumbered). The offset was confirmed against four TOC entries. The document prints no page numbers (H2), so citations derive from the TOC and measured heading positions.
- All 38 TOC page references were checked against measured heading positions; every one landed correctly.
- P&L benefit rows, cost rows, net benefit, cumulative net benefit and the ROI percentage were recomputed independently and all tie exactly.
- I have not verified whether the POV size and scope were agreed with Phill, nor whether USD is AUB's declared reporting currency — it is almost certainly right for a US-chartered university in a dollarised economy, and only one currency is used anywhere in the document, but there is no front matter to confirm it against (H6).

## Vendors included in the proposal

The report carries no appendix "Vendors and Third-Party Components". This list is my sweep of the document text and has not been reconciled against any list the consultant holds, nor against the architecture diagrams I cannot read.

| Vendor | Product or component | Role in the proposed solution | Commercial status | Printed pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3Point | 3AIgent RAG and Agentic Platform; delivery and advisory | AI orchestration, RAG, POV and production delivery, platform training | Included in quoted pricing — subscription USD 80,000 p.a. (USD 320,000 over four years); implementation USD 315,333; training USD 4,050; POV USD 30,600 | 8, 15, 22, 25–26 |
| Cisco | AI POD; UCS C845A M8 servers; Intersight; AI Defense; Hypershield; Isovalent; Nexus switching | On-premises GPU compute, infrastructure management, model, application and network security | Included in quoted pricing — Capex USD 1,720,240 plus installation USD 40,000. The "Opex, subscriptions, upgrades and support" line is costed at **zero** across all five years | 15–20, 33–35 |
| NVIDIA | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 96 GB — 2 for the POV, 4 in production | GPU acceleration for inference, RAG, embedding and reranking | **Unclear** — not itemised; presumed inside the Cisco Capex line but never stated. Named as an engagement party in the running header of all 38 pages | 20, 33–35, header on 1–38 |
| Ellucian | Banner (system of record); Ellucian Experience / AUB Nexus; Degree Completion | Authoritative student, course, registration and eligibility data; the student-facing portal the assistant is embedded in | Client existing estate. No line for API/Ethos licensing or Ellucian professional services; integration effort presumed inside the 3Point line | 3, 12–13, 17–20, 23, 26, 33 |
| Microsoft | Entra ID / SSO; SharePoint | Authentication and identity context; source of advising documents for the RAG corpus | Client existing estate | 12, 17–20, 23, 26, 33 |
| Red Hat | OpenShift — named only as "Kubernetes / OpenShift" | Container platform for the AI POD, in both the POV and production configurations | **Not named as a vendor and nowhere costed.** p. 20 records it as "Existing platform or POV configuration"; if new, a licensed subscription falls outside the p. 15 figures | 18–20, 26, 35 |
| Unnamed | Vector database / knowledge index | Stores embeddings for the RAG corpus; an explicit line in both the POV and production configurations | Not named, not costed | 17, 19–20, 35 |
| Unnamed | Primary LLM (8B–14B class, optionally ~32B); embedding model; reranker | Response generation, retrieval and ranking | No provider named; no licence, hosting or model line in the p. 15 costs | 20, 34–35 |

**Vendor costs not covered by the Section 5.1 figures, and not flagged as such.** Three. Red Hat OpenShift is required by both the POV and production configurations and appears in no cost line. The vector database is a sized, scheduled configuration component with no cost. Ellucian API licensing and any Ellucian professional-services effort for the Banner and Nexus integrations are nowhere in the p. 15 breakdown, although that integration is central to the solution and sits on the POV critical path. Separately and more visibly, the Cisco "Opex, subscriptions, upgrades and support" line is carried at zero for four years against a USD 1,720,240 platform — the report should either state what is bundled into the Capex line and for how long, or price the support.

**Components described only by category where a vendor has evidently been assumed.** The vector database (pp. 17, 19–20, 35) is sized and scheduled — "Vector DB requirement <1 TB initially, expandable" — so a product is in mind. The LLM is specified by parameter class and benchmarked against a "70B-class" alternative (p. 34), which implies a chosen model family. Both need naming, or an explicit statement that the choice is open and cost-neutral.

**Consolidating appendix.** Absent (B7). When writing it, note that NVIDIA appears in the running header of every page as an engagement party — "3Point/Cisco/Nvidia" — while being invisible in every commercial table. Procurement will read that as a party to the deal and ask what is being bought from them.

# Compliance review — DVZ-MV Final Report (draft)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Customer** | DVZ-MV |
| **Document reviewed** | DVZ-MV REPORT DRAFT.pdf — 39 PDF pages / 38 printed pages, exported 13 October 2026 |
| **Template** | `report/final_report_template_v1.md` |
| **Review date** | 13 October 2026 |
| **Page numbering** | Printed = PDF − 1, confirmed against every TOC entry from §2 (p. 3) to 9.7 (p. 38). No page prints a number |
| **Verdict** | **Not ready for peer review** — 8 blocking issues: the ROI is below the band on an unvalidated, incomplete model, and the PoV is not sized or defined |

## Summary

The argument is clear and well built. One use case is explained as three connected parts, with the human decision points stated plainly (pp. 3–4, 10–11). The driver arithmetic is shown in full and reconciles to the P&L (pp. 13, 27–29), and overlaps between drivers are excluded. The draft is candid that a simulated PoV proves behaviour, not savings (p. 22).

Eight issues block peer review. The ROI is 72%, below the 100% floor, and falls further once a Year 1 ramp is applied (B1). Every volume is "illustrative" and nothing is signed off (B2). The cost base is unfinished — infra sizing reads "TODO CISCO" (B3). The PoV has no day size, effort profile or commercial basis (B4), no deliverables table (B5) and no success criteria table (B6); its scope needs an agreed exception (B7). There is no vendor appendix (B8).

## Blocking issues

### B1 — The ROI is 72%, below the 100% floor, and assumes full benefit from Year 1

**Rule.** The first use case lands between 100% and 300%. Below 100%: do not inflate; revisit the scope, check for omitted benefits, escalate to the engagement lead and report the honest figure. Year 1 benefit is ramped at about 50%.

**Evidence.** The P&L ties: €2,235,600 benefit, €1,301,318 cost, €934,282 net, 72% (p. 13). The figure is reported honestly and identically on pp. 3 and 13. But "Full annual benefits assumed from Year 1 of production, with no adoption or implementation ramp-up" (p. 15), which note 5 calls "a conservative steady-state production scenario" (p. 14). The PoV cost is excluded (F3) and the cost base is incomplete (B3).

On the report's own figures, including the €27,360 PoV gives 68%; a 50% Year 1 ramp gives 55% (benefit €2,012,040, net €710,722); both give 51% [my calculations].

**Fix.** Escalate to Mike before peer review. Two legitimate routes, neither of which is raising a rate or a percentage:
- Omitted benefits. Benefit 1 "excludes any additional financial value associated with reduced network downtime or improved SLA performance" (p. 27). Add it as a fifth driver: `[NEEDS INPUT: annual downtime hours and cost per hour, or SLA penalties, from DVZ-MV Network Services]`.
- Scope. 3Point implementation is €624,091, 48% of total cost. Test a narrower first production slice with Mike: `[NEEDS INPUT: implementation estimate for reconciliation and read-only assistance on a bounded network scope]`.
- If it stays under 100%, report it as such, apply the ramp, and delete "conservative" from note 5.

### B2 — The drivers are arithmetically sound, but every volume is "illustrative" and nothing is signed off

**Rule.** Every figure and assumption is confirmed by named customer staff with dates, in the appendix "ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off". Drivers rest on customer denominators.

**Evidence.** All four calculations are shown and correct (pp. 27–29). Their inputs are not DVZ-MV's:

- 900 incidents: "Illustrative assumption pending confirmation"; 2,000 records: "Illustrative workload assumption"; 40 engineers: "Illustrative adoption assumption"; 3,000 diagnostic tasks: no source given (all p. 14).
- €135 an hour: "To be validated", and taken from a project rate given in the workshop (p. 14).

The only customer-sourced figures are the estate counts (14,000 switches, 553 routers, 553 firewalls, 640 schools, p. 14), which no driver uses. The Validation row lists everything as requiring "DVZ-MV confirmation" (p. 15). The appendix is absent (pp. 27–38 searched), as are both validation statements.

**Fix.** Replace each input: `[NEEDS INPUT: annual incident count from Spectrum or the service desk; records verified; standalone diagnostic tasks; NOC headcount; loaded internal hourly cost — from DVZ-MV Network Services/NOC and Finance]`. Add the appendix with one row per input and cost line, marked outstanding until confirmed. Check whether €135 is a charge-out rate; an internal loaded rate would be the correct value for released capacity.

### B3 — The cost base is unfinished

**Rule.** Full five-year recurring and support costs; client-side effort included; hardware lines name vendor and product; Infra Sizing carries the configuration; any FX rate is stated once with its date.

**Evidence.**
- "Cisco AI Platform, subscriptions, upgrades and support" is €185,180 in Year 1 and blank in Years 2–5 (p. 13).
- 9.4 Infra sizing reads, in full, "TODO CISCO" (p. 35). Note 2 says infrastructure and recurring costs "are TBC" (p. 14).
- No DVZ-MV effort line, although §9.5 identifies skills development in six areas (p. 35) and §2.3 asks for nominated experts (p. 5).
- "FX rate £ to €: 1.2 Euro (Illustrative)" (p. 14): no date, and an illustrative rate makes every converted line unauditable.

**Fix.** Obtain the Cisco configuration and five-year pricing: `[NEEDS INPUT: bill of materials and Years 2–5 subscription and support, from the Cisco account team]`. Add a client-effort line: `[NEEDS INPUT: DVZ-MV days for experts, integration owners and training]`. Replace note 4 with "Costs incurred in GBP are converted at GBP 1 = EUR `[rate]`, taken on `[DD Month YYYY]`." Re-run B1 afterwards; every one of these lowers the ROI.

### B4 — The PoV is four weeks and €27,360, but has no day size, effort profile or commercial basis

**Rule.** §7.1 states effort (20 or 40 days), elapsed duration, team, commercial basis and environment; §2.2, §2.3 and §8.1 repeat the day size. Size and scope are agreed with Phill before peer review.

**Evidence.** The four-week schedule is clear and well structured, week by week (pp. 21–22). The P&L carries "Proof of Value €27,360" in a "POV 2026" column (p. 13). No page states days, a team, who pays, or where it runs; the p. 31 diagram says "Hosting and sizing to be confirmed" (read by eye).

**Fix.** Add the "PoV at a glance" table to §7.1 and an effort profile summing to the size; the four weekly rows on pp. 21–22 map directly onto workstreams. Commercial basis in the template's neutral wording: `[NEEDS INPUT: size, price and commercial basis as agreed with Phill]`.

### B5 — PoV outputs are named in one sentence; there is no deliverables table

**Rule.** Mandatory in §7.1: receivable artefacts, each with a format and named recipient, each backed by days, ending with the PoV outcome report and production recommendation.

**Evidence.** "The delivery team will provide the demonstrated workflows, an explanation of the simulation boundaries and a summary of feedback, dependencies and requirements for a live implementation" (p. 22). No format, recipient or outcome report appears on pp. 4–5 or 21–25.

**Fix.** Build the table from that sentence and the weekly outcomes:

| # | Deliverable | Format | Received by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Synthetic network, documents and simulated interfaces | Data set in the PoV environment | `[NEEDS INPUT: DVZ-MV role]` |
| 2 | Working demonstration: retrieval, reconciliation, Webchat, playbooks, root cause analysis | Working software in `[NEEDS INPUT: environment]` | `[NEEDS INPUT]` |

Every converted figure must reconcile to the single stated rate. Four of the five CAPEX lines on p. 19 do: £182,156 → €218,588, £277,110 → €332,532, £9,413 → €11,295, £40,000 → €48,000, all at 1.2. "Cisco Hardware & Software (Full)" shows £488,400 → €567,600, a rate of 1.162. The €18,480 difference propagates onto the same page: the cost breakdown totals €1,178,015 while the P&L row above it shows €1,196,495 for the same CAPEX. The €1.6m headline uses the second figure, so the business case is unaffected — but two different euro totals for one cost appear on one page.

**Action:** establish which currency Cisco quoted in, restate the line, and make both totals agree.

### B3 — Figures are recorded as requiring Končar's confirmation, not as confirmed by it

Customer sign-off is mandatory before issue, recorded in the appendix "ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off". The report takes the opposite position: "Deployment volumes, margins, labour rates, inventory values and bid conversion assumptions require confirmation by Končar" (p. 19). No sign-off appendix exists, and no named Končar person or date appears anywhere in 45 pages. One assumption is genuinely customer-derived — the "€20–€40 hourly cost range discussed during the workshop" (p. 19). Everything else rests on assumed volumes with no stated denominator: 3 pilots in Year 1, 2 deployments a year after, one additional win per year, and an inventory reduction of £250,000 then £500,000 a year against a total inventory value that is never given.

**Action:** hold the validation session, record it in a new appendix with names and dates, and give the inventory driver a denominator. Until then the front matter cannot read higher than Draft.

### B4 — The two PoVs are described but not sized, priced, gated or given deliverables

The deliverables table and the success criteria table are both mandatory content in §7.1, and neither may be deferred to a later document.

What the PoVs would prove is specified, and specified well: the central PoV covers simulations triggered from the edge, model training and push to edge, and digital workers for central control activities; the edge PoV covers alert-time root cause analysis, procedure suggestion, remediation scheduling, and human-approved central simulation requests (pp. 24–25). Missing is everything a funder needs — day size, elapsed duration, team, environment, in-scope and out-of-scope lists, deliverables with formats and named recipients, an effort profile that sums to the size, success criteria with baselines and targets, and a decision gate.

Two departures look deliberate. The template expects one PoV as a subset of the number one use case; two follow logically from the central-plus-edge architecture. And "which after approval can be sponsored by Cisco" (p. 24) is properly hedged and does not assert funding. Both need Phill's agreement as a recorded exception.

**Action:** size both PoVs in days, add the deliverables and success criteria tables, and confirm the two-PoV shape with Phill before this goes to peer review.

### B5 — Benefit 1's recurring-licence column total is £220,000 short of its own rows

The recurring licences and services column on p. 16 runs £20,000, £80,000, £120,000, £160,000, £200,000 — £580,000 — but the five-year total row states £360,000. The three column totals therefore sum to £1,460,000 against a stated £1,680,000. The £1,680,000 is correct and is what carries into the P&L, so the headline is unaffected. It is a wrong number in a table the customer will add up.

**Action:** correct the subtotal to £580,000.

### B6 — Three different recommended next steps

Section 2.3 recommends "a short joint research and development phase" with six activities ending in a customer demonstrator (p. 5). Section 7.2 proposes two Proofs of Value (p. 24). Section 8.2 lists "Agree the strategic collaboration model" first and "Run the two proofs of value" second (p. 29). Section 2.2 adds a fourth framing: "an R&D phase where an end-to-end demo is built" (p. 5). A reader cannot tell what Končar is being asked to approve; the template's position is that the recommended next step is always the PoV, stated identically in §2.3, §7.1 and §8.

**Action:** pick one — the two PoVs, on the evidence of §7.2 — and make §2.2, §2.3 and §8.2 say it.

### B7 — No vendor appendix, and two vendors appear only inside a cost line

"Vendors and Third-Party Components" is a mandatory appendix and the single list procurement works from. It is absent, and the sweep at the end of this review found two names the narrative never mentions: **ABB**, in "Integrations: Digital Twins, ABB & Končar control centre, simulations" (p. 19), and **Industrial-X**, in "Create Končar-X on top of Industrial-X" (p. 19) — a platform the entire £182,156 build sits on, with no owner, description or reference anywhere else. The P&L also books a "3rd Party Products £0 / €0" line (p. 19), asserting there is no third-party product spend, while the architecture calls for a language model, a vector index and SCADA/historian connectors (pp. 35–36, 39) — none named, none costed.

**Action:** add the appendix using the table at the end of this review, describe Industrial-X, and either cost the model and index or say in the narrative why they are zero.

### B8 — The Cisco Secure AI Factory is never named, and the platform economics are never quantified

For Cisco engagements the Secure AI Factory must be named as the platform for the whole portfolio, with increasing platform value and falling incremental delivery cost both stated **and quantified** in a §6.1 economics table. The platform argument is made repeatedly — reuse across customers and asset types (p. 5), "a platform that becomes stronger and faster to deploy with every customer project" (p. 23) — and Cisco's components are named: secure AI PODs, Cisco Unified Edge (pp. 24, 40). But "Cisco Secure AI Factory" appears nowhere in 45 pages, and no figure attaches to the reuse claim: no one-time foundation cost, no per-deployment incremental cost, no reduction percentage. The report also never states how many use cases exist, so the "all N use cases" framing has nothing to attach to.

**Action:** name the Cisco Secure AI Factory in §2 and §6, and build the §6.1 economics table by splitting the p. 19 CAPEX into one-time foundation cost and per-deployment cost.

### B9 — Infra sizing is a placeholder with a live internal link

Appendix 9.2 reads in full: "Cisco to complete", followed by a live `netorgft17315613.sharepoint.com` URL (p. 43). The link points into 3Point's own SharePoint tenant and must not reach the customer. **Action:** complete the sizing or remove the appendix and its TOC entry. Remove the URL either way.

## Section-by-section findings

**§2 Executive Summary (pp. 3–5) — F11.** The business case narrative is strong and correctly leads with the structural problem rather than the technology. Absent: the thank-you callout, the strategic pillars table, the value-unlocks list, and the numbered next-steps table with owners and timeframes. Also B6, X4, X5.

**§3 Current State (pp. 5–7) — F3.** Both subsections are argued in prose, and the nine objectives on pp. 7–8 are specific and well drawn. Neither mandatory table is present — no challenge table with urgency and cost of inaction, no objective-to-use-case mapping. Urgency is correctly kept qualitative here, with quantified framing held back to §5.2.

**§4.1 Use Case Identification (p. 7) — F1.** Six selection criteria are given and they are good ones. Genuinely absent, searched across §4 and all of §9: any count of candidate use cases submitted, the funnel table, the portfolio summary table, and any acknowledgement of what Končar's people contributed. The report never states how many use cases exist, which is also why B8 cannot be written as the template asks.

**§4.2 Selected Priority Use Cases (pp. 8–14) — F2.** Seven pages against a 2.5-page budget, and the best-written part of the document — the transformer temperature alarm walkthrough (p. 11) and the transformer overheating playbook (p. 14) are exactly the right level of concreteness. None of it is in the required shape: no target users, key dependencies, expected outcomes, business value statement, PoV subset marker, user interfaces table or solution design table. Most of pp. 12–14 is solution design that belongs in the Technical Architecture appendix, where much of it already appears.

**§5.1 ROI and Payback (pp. 14–19) — F4, F5, F6.** Also B1, B2, B3, B5.
- **F4:** the subsection is titled "ROI and Payback" and the model shows cumulative net benefit turning positive in Year 3 (p. 19). Payback is never stated. The word appears twice in the document, both times in that heading.
- **F5:** the P&L on p. 19 is an embedded spreadsheet object, not a native table — its text sits inside a Form XObject with its own coordinate system, and it renders at 10 pt and 11 pt where the surrounding tables are 9 pt. A reviewer cannot edit it and the header row will not repeat across a page break. The three standing notes are present and verbatim.
- **F6:** "The benefits have been estimated under a conservative scenario" (p. 15), and each driver argues its own conservatism honestly. The mechanism is what is missing: no benefit realisation percentage is stated; the Year-1 50% ramp is applied to Benefit 3 (£25,000 against £50,000) but not to Benefits 4 or 5, and the assumptions state plainly "Benefits are assumed to start in Year 1"; and client-side effort — Končar engineering time, change management, data remediation — appears nowhere in the £1.2m CAPEX. At 152% the ROI is inside the band, so none of this needs to move the number. It needs to be stated.

**§5.2 Risks of Inaction (pp. 20–21) — F7.** Thirteen well-drawn risks with consequence, business impact and indicative timing, framed as value forgone rather than loss incurred exactly as the template asks, and correctly separating the working-capital item as cash flow rather than recurring P&L benefit. Two departures: the template asks for 3–5 risks, and none carries a quantified annual cost of inaction despite the model on the facing pages supplying the numbers.

**§6 Target AI Platform (pp. 22–23) — B8.** The architecture principles are not set out as principles, though most are argued inside the narrative. The EU AI Act, Cyber Resilience Act and NIS2 framing (p. 23) is a good addition the template does not ask for and should be kept.

**§7 Implementation Roadmap (pp. 23–28) — F8.** Six pages against three. The seven-phase structure is coherent and the three-way collaboration model (p. 24) is a legitimate reframing of the engagement that the template does not anticipate — worth agreeing as an exception rather than correcting, and it may be the template that should change. But no phase carries a duration, a milestone list or an entry condition, and skills and resistance to change are not addressed at all. The roadmap cannot be planned against as written.

**§8 Conclusion (pp. 29–30) — F9.** Five recommendations and six immediate actions, all specific. The actions are a numbered list with no owners and no deadlines, and confirmation of the ROI figures — which the template fixes as the first action — is not among them. The missing financial figure is X4.

**§9 Appendices (pp. 31–45) — F10.** Numbered 9.1–9.4 with TOC entries, where the template requires unnumbered labels and no TOC entry. Four of ten template appendices are present and three of those four are strong. Six are absent: Detailed Financial Models, ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off, POV Scope and Work Breakdown, Use Case Detail Sheets, Vendors and Third-Party Components, Analyst Sources and Benchmarks. The financial detail is not missing — it is in the main body on pp. 16–19, which is a large part of X1. No analyst source other than Eurostat (p. 19) is cited anywhere.

**Front matter (cover) — F12.** The cover carries title, subtitle, abstract and two authors. No generation date, no version, no review status. Classification appears as "Commercial in Confidence" in the running header rather than in the front matter, which is acceptable in substance. The title reads "AI Realisation Assessment"; the template's is "AI Readiness Assessment".

## Cross-cutting findings

**X1 — Main body is 30 pages against a ~20-page budget.** From the TOC page references: §1 2pp (budget 1), §2 2pp (3), §3 2pp (2), §4 7pp (4), §5 8pp (3), §6 1pp (2), §7 6pp (3), §8 2pp (2). §4, §5 and §7 carry the whole overrun; §2, §3, §6 and §8 are inside budget. The fix is relocation, not deletion: the benefit derivation tables (pp. 16–19) belong in "Detailed Financial Models" and the solution design on pp. 12–14 in "Technical Architecture".

**X2 — Sections 3, 4, 5 and 7 do not start on a new page.** §3 opens at the foot of p. 5, §4 mid p. 7, §5 mid p. 14, §7 at the foot of p. 23. §2, §6, §8 and §9 do start at the top of a page (pp. 3, 22, 29, 31), so the rule is applied inconsistently rather than not at all. No stray blank pages found in 46 PDF pages.

**X3 — No MANDATORY or HIGHLIGHT content anywhere; the draft appears to be written against the older template.** None of the template's mandatory callouts appears, in any wording. Nor do any of the v1-specific requirements: the reporting currency rule, the long-list funnel, the vendor appendix, the ROI validation appendix, the PoV at §7.1, unnumbered appendices. Section numbering for §2–§6 and §8 matches, which is common to both templates. This single fact explains B4, B7, F1, F10, F11 and much of B3 at once, and is a more useful thing to fix than any of them individually. Inferred from the absence of v1-only features; I did not have the older template file to compare against.

**X4 — The headline net benefit is given twice, differently, and is absent from §8.** Page 4: "an illustrative five-year net benefit of approximately €2.4 million". Page 15: "an estimated five-year net benefit of €2.5 million". The model gives €2,474,844 (p. 19), so p. 15 is right. Page 4 is also inconsistent within its own sentence: €4.1m less €1.6m is €2.5m. The 152% ROI is stated identically in both places, but §8 carries no financial figure at all, where the template requires the headline in §2, §2.1, §5.1 and §8.

**X5 — Two pieces of the value argument exist only inside images.** "The proposed solution generates value through six principal mechanisms:" (p. 4) is followed by a diagram, and "these benefits contribute to generate value in three levels" (p. 15) likewise. Neither the six mechanisms nor the three levels appears as text anywhere in the document. They cannot be searched, quoted into a deck, or checked against §5.1's five value drivers — five drivers against six mechanisms is a discrepancy no reader can resolve.

## House style and typography

Measured from the embedded font resources and the text-rendering operators. Aptos is present and is the body face throughout at 12 pt: the base is right, and the drift is at the edges.

| ID | Element | Measured | House style |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Cover title / abstract | Calibri 36 pt / Calibri 14 pt | Aptos Display 28 pt bold / Aptos 12 pt |
| H2 | Running header | Aptos 10 pt; no footer and no page number on any page | Aptos 9 pt |
| H3 | §6 heading (p. 22); §3.2 and §7.3 (pp. 6, 25) | Aptos 20 pt / Aptos 16 pt | Aptos Display |
| H3 | §4.2.2.1–4.2.2.8 (pp. 9–14) | Aptos Italic 12 pt | Aptos 14 pt bold |

Arial and Times New Roman are declared in the font resources but carry no visible text, with one exception: a Times New Roman Bold full stop on p. 14 (E8). No caption style — Aptos 9 pt italic — is used anywhere, and the strings "Figure" and "Table *n*" do not appear, which is why H6 reads as absent rather than incomplete. UK English is consistent throughout; no US spellings found. "Končar" is spelled identically 154 times.

## Editorial defects

| ID | Page | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 2, 5 | "Current State and Strategic Drives" | "Drivers", in the heading and the TOC |
| E2 | 18 | "£121,000 × 1.1 = £133,00" | £133,100, or restate |
| E3 | 18 | Narrative says "5% annual growth"; the table applies 10% | Reconcile — the £610,000 total assumes 10% |
| E4 | 18 | Year 5 shown as £146,000; 133,000 × 1.1 = £146,300 | Restate or state the rounding |
| E5 | 4 | "€4.1 millions of gross value" | "€4.1 million" |
| E6 | 9 | "See a non-functional demo at koncar.3aigent.com" | Decide before issue — live 3Point-hosted link |
| E7 | throughout | "Končar's" with both straight and curly apostrophes | One form |
| E8 | 14 | Times New Roman Bold full stop | Reapply the body style |
| E9 | 3 | "9.2 Infra sizing" and "9.3 Stakeholder and change assessment" against "9.1 Technical Architecture" and "9.4 KPI Catalogue" | One case convention |

## What is working well

- The five value drivers are each derived rather than asserted, with visible arithmetic (pp. 16–19). Every per-driver table ties, the P&L ties year by year, and 151.69% is correctly computed as five-year net benefit over five-year total cost.
- 152% lands inside the 100–300% guardrail with no haircut needed — the hardest thing to get right first time.
- The engineering rate is traced to the workshop, cross-checked against Eurostat, and the report says openly that it took the upper end of the €20–€40 range (p. 19).
- The technical architecture appendix (pp. 31–43) separates read-only intelligence integration from control action integration and holds critical actions for human approval — the right instinct for critical infrastructure, and unprompted by the template.
- The risks-of-inaction table (pp. 20–21) frames every risk as value forgone rather than loss incurred, and correctly marks the inventory item as a cash-flow effect rather than a recurring P&L benefit.
- The stakeholder matrix (pp. 44–45) is populated with real Končar groups in all four quadrants, not placeholders.

## Method and limitations

- Text, fonts, font sizes and per-page image resources extracted with `pypdf` 6.14.2. Poppler is not installed, so no page was rendered.
- **I cannot see images.** Five figures (pp. 4, 9, 15, 22, 31) and the cover were not read. Nothing about their content is asserted here; where a diagram plainly carries vendor names I have said so rather than guessed.
- Printed page numbers are derived as PDF page minus one, confirmed at four TOC anchors (§2 p. 3, §5 p. 14, §8 p. 29, §9 p. 31). The document prints no page number on any page, so the TOC is the only source for its own numbering.
- The P&L on p. 19 is an embedded object; its text extracts without layout, so its figures were reconciled by value rather than by cell position. All arithmetic in B2 and B5 was recomputed independently.
- X3 is inferred from the absence of v1-only features, not verified against the older template file.
- Before declaring anything absent I searched the whole document for its substance rather than its heading. F1, H6 and B8 were each confirmed by content search across all 46 pages.

## Vendors included in the proposal

The report carries no "Vendors and Third-Party Components" appendix (B7). This sweep covers the narrative, the cost breakdown, the architecture appendix and the KPI catalogue.

| Vendor | Product or component | Role in the proposed solution | Commercial status | Printed pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3Point | 3AIgent — digital worker, agentic and RAG platform | Application intelligence layer on which Končar builds its digital worker solutions | Included in quoted pricing — £72,500 / €87,000 annual OPEX | 4, 5, 19, 24, 26, 27, 28 |
| 3Point | Delivery and advisory services | Solution design, PoV delivery, platform build | Included in quoted pricing | 5, 19, 24–28 |
| Cisco | Secure AI PODs | Central platform compute | Included in quoted pricing — "Cisco Hardware & Software (Full)" £488,400 / €567,600 | 19, 24 |
| Cisco | Unified Edge | Edge infrastructure for brownfield and greenfield sites | Included in the line above | 19, 23, 24, 40 |
| Cisco | Networking, cybersecurity, factory-ready deployment | Secure infrastructure foundation and container pre-integration | Included in quoted pricing — "Cisco Installation" £40,000 / €48,000 | 5, 19, 24, 27, 28 |
| Končar | Končar-X, built on Industrial-X | The industrial AI product being created | Included in quoted pricing — £182,156 / €218,588 CAPEX | 19 |
| Končar | Factory-built container units | Pre-integrated greenfield edge deployment | Not costed — commercialisation model, not this proposal | 23, 40 |
| Industrial-X | Platform Končar-X is built on top of | Underlying platform for the build | Included in the Končar-X CAPEX line; owner and description not stated anywhere | 19 |
| ABB | Control centre system | Integration target alongside the Končar control centre and digital twins | Assumed client existing estate — the integration effort is in the £277,110 / €332,532 CAPEX line, ABB-side licensing is not | 19 |
| Microsoft | SharePoint | Not part of the solution — a 3Point-internal document link left in appendix 9.2 | n/a — remove (B9) | 43 |

**Vendor costs not covered by the Section 5.1 figures, and not flagged as such in the report.** The P&L books a "3rd Party Products £0 / €0" line (p. 19). Against the architecture on pp. 35–39 that is not credible: nothing is costed for the language model or its inference, the vector and keyword index, SCADA/DCS/historian connector licensing, or ABB-side integration licensing. None of these is flagged as client-procured either. The zero line asserts there is no third-party product spend without the narrative ever saying so.

**Components named only by category where a specific vendor has evidently been assumed.**
- The language or foundation model behind RAG answer generation (pp. 11, 35–36) — no provider named anywhere in 45 pages.
- The vector database and hybrid index (p. 35) — "vector search" only.
- GPU and AI compute inside the Cisco AI PODs and the edge devices (pp. 22, 23, 40) — NVIDIA is never named.
- SCADA, DCS, EMS and historian (pp. 33–34, 39) — categories throughout. ABB is the only product name in the document, and it appears solely in a cost line.
- "Digital Twins" as a costed integration target (p. 19) — no product named.

**Vendors possibly named in artwork I cannot read.** The architecture diagrams on pp. 22 and 31, and the figures on pp. 4, 9 and 15, are images. Diagrams of this kind routinely carry vendor logos and product names. They must be swept by eye before this list is treated as complete.

**Appendix coverage.** There is no vendors appendix, so nothing was missed against it — the table above is the first consolidated list, and ABB and Industrial-X would not have reached procurement without it.

**Action:** state what the €140,742 buys and for how long; split hardware CAPEX from annual OPEX; carry OPEX across all five years; recompute.

"Proof of Value - Corporate Knowledge Base", €36,000, and "AI Solution Implementation 3Point - Corporate Knowledge Base", €312,300 (p. 15). The use case is Competitor Pricing Analysis. Either the labels were carried over from another report, or the prices were. Together they are 69% of total cost.

The report says the opposite, candidly: the model "remains subject to validation through the Proof of Value" (p. 14). No sign-off appendix exists and no MaxiDi name or date appears on any page. The €2,800,422,784 revenue base is taken from Aziende.it, with the open caveat "Confirm whether the full legal-entity revenue should be used" (p. 33). The 0.10%, 0.15%, 40%, 25% and 20% factors are 3Point assumptions (p. 21).

This looks deliberate: the PoV exists to measure the value. That is a decision needing an agreed exception with Mike, not an oversight. Next step 4 already asks Finance to agree the attribution basis (p. 5).

**Action:** have MaxiDi Finance confirm the revenue perimeter and the 35% figure now, record names and dates in the new appendix, and mark the remaining factors as outstanding.

## Blocking issues

This is a known, deliberate position. The printed comments record the question and the answer: the solution "requires significant infrastructure for the complexity" (p. 3). So it needs a decision, not a correction. Two things make that decision harder than 22% suggests. The cost is 49% Cisco platform (€667,683 of €1,371,333, p. 16), bought for one use case with a nil portfolio value beside it (F12). And 22% is not yet conservative: see X2 and F2.

### B2 — The headline net benefit and ROI do not tie, and a second benefit schedule contradicts the P&L

The driver arithmetic ties, and so do the cost columns (pp. 16–18). Two things do not.

| Item | Report says | Recomputed |

| Net benefit, 5 years | €381,957 / "€382k" (pp. 3, 16) | €1,679,040 − €1,371,333 = **€307,707**. The net row sums Years 1–5 and leaves out the €74,250 PoV column |
| ROI | 22% (pp. 3, 16) | €307,707 ÷ €1,371,333 = 22%. Correct, but €382k would be 28% |
| Benefit, Years 2–5 | €394,800 a year; five-year €1,859,040 (p. 18) | €349,800 a year; €1,679,040 (p. 16, and "≈ €349,800" on p. 18 itself) |

**Action:** state the net benefit as €307,707 everywhere, and correct the p. 18 schedule.

### B3 — Every benefit driver is an illustrative assumption, and validation is deferred to the pilot

Customer sign-off is mandatory and recorded in the appendix "ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off". The report takes the opposite position, candidly: the assumptions "are not a confirmed forecast" and stand "pending pilot validation" (p. 17). §8.1 recommends using "measured pilot results to validate the ROI assumptions" (p. 24). No sign-off appendix exists, and no Milano Serravalle name or date appears on any page.

The financial case holds together. The P&L reconciles to €9,250,225 net and 127% ROI, inside the band, with payback correctly read as Year 3 (pp. 16–17).
