**Evidence.** Timing is clear: weeks 1–2 to scope and prepare, weeks 3–6 for the hosted PoV, with a pass condition (p. 21). The P&L image shows "Proof of Value – VLAM Digital Workers 26,700" in red (p. 17). No page states days — the only "days" in §7 is the 10-working-day decision window (p. 21). No text states a price or who pays. The printed comments show the days were requested and then held back: "added the estimates to the internal spreadsheet… We normally don't share those with the customer" (p. 21).

**Action.** Add the "PoV at a glance" table and an effort profile that sums to the stated size. State the commercial basis in the template's neutral wording. €26,700 is $30,000 at the report's own implied rate (X3), which matches the Cisco budget in the comment on p. 21 [inferred] — so confirm with Phill before the figure stays in.

### B2 — PoV outputs are named in prose, but there is no deliverables table

**Rule.** The §7.1 deliverables table is mandatory: receivable artefacts, each with a format and a named recipient, each backed by days, ending with the PoV outcome report and production recommendation.

**Evidence.** Outputs are described as "tangible demos of the selected processes, stakeholder feedback and a clearer understanding of the requirements" (p. 22) and as activities in the phase table (p. 21). Step 5 on p. 6 uses "the findings" but no outcome report is named. No format or recipient appears in pp. 5–6 or 21–22.

**Action.** Build the table from what is already implied: three configured digital workers in the hosted environment, the synthetic test set, the scored Table A results, the pilot design, and the outcome report.

### B3 — The PoV demonstrates all three processes on synthetic data; the template asks for a subset on the customer's own data

**Rule.** The PoV is "never the whole use case" and proves the value hypothesis "on the customer's own data".

**Evidence.** This is a deliberate choice, openly made. The PoV covers Purchase Approvals, Service Desk and TRA (pp. 5, 10) "on synthetic data and simulated integrations" in a hosted environment (p. 14). The draft says what that costs: the realised share "will be measured in the controlled pilot, because the hosted Proof of Value uses synthetic data and cannot measure it" (p. 16), and it separates the "distinct forms of evidence" of PoV and pilot (p. 5).

**Action.** Not an error to correct but an exception to agree. Record Phill's and Mike's agreement that a capability demonstration is the right first step for a sovereignty-bound customer, and say in §7 why. If this pattern will recur, the template needs a "hosted demonstration" variant. Three workers in four weeks also needs testing against the 20-day size (B1).

**Rule.** Every figure and assumption is confirmed by named customer staff with dates, in the appendix "ROI Validation and Customer Sign-Off". The first next-step row is always that sign-off.

**Evidence.** Customer denominators are present throughout: €300,000,000 of purchases, 30 new TRAs plus 10 reviews, 300,000 contacts (p. 16), described as "SSC-ICT's own estimates". **Action.** Add the appendix with one row per driver and cost line, marked outstanding where they are. Put ROI sign-off first in §2.3 and §8.2. Resolve F2 and F3 before the figures go to SSC-ICT.

## 2. Executive Summary

> [!MANDATORY]
> 3Point and Cisco would like to thank the members of SSC-ICT who have worked with us on this AI Readiness Assessment. It has been a pleasure to work with you and we wish you all the very best for your AI journey.

> [!HIGHLIGHT]
> Our modelling estimates that VLAM Digital Workers will return €4,908,483 to SSC-ICT over 5 years (293% ROI). It combines SSC-ICT's three selected use cases, so the portfolio total is the same: €4,908,483 (293%).

The table below gives the headline figures.

**VLAM Digital Workers at a glance**

| Metric | EUR |
|---|---|
| Total benefits (5 years) | €6,581,250 |
| Total costs (5 years) | €1,672,767 |
| Net benefit (5 years) | €4,908,483 |
| Return on investment (5 years) | 293% |
| Payback | under 12 months |

> [!MANDATORY]
> Return on Investment (ROI) analysis was completed by 3Point using validated financial data reviewed and confirmed as accurate by SSC-ICT staff. We have listed assumptions and benchmarks from industry research in this document.

> [!MANDATORY]
> The recommended path is to focus first on a proof of value scoped as a subset of VLAM Digital Workers, establish the operating model and data foundations, and then scale in a disciplined way across the broader portfolio.

VLAM Digital Workers is one AI assistant serving Purchase Approvals, Technical Risk Analysis (TRA) and the Service Desk Chatbot. It drafts and checks forms and answers routine questions, while approvers, security advisers and service desk agents keep every decision.

It runs on Cisco Secure AI Factory, Cisco's validated on-premises AI infrastructure built from AI PODs (pre-sized compute, network and storage blocks) in SSC-ICT's own data centre. It uses 3AIgent, 3Point's platform that grounds answers in SSC-ICT's documents and runs workflow steps. The platform serves the whole portfolio, so each added use case raises its value and lowers incremental cost (Section 6.1).

### 2.1 A Compelling Business Case

Over five years, VLAM Digital Workers is modelled to deliver €4,908,483 net, an ROI of 293%, with benefits counted well below SSC-ICT's own gross estimates (Section 5.1). Cisco platform, Proof of Value and SSC-ICT internal costs are still to be priced and will lower the return. The value unlocks are:

- €450,000 a year in price rises and lost offers avoided
- €184,500 a year of security-adviser time released
- €828,000 a year of service-desk contacts resolved by the assistant

### 2.2 Recommended Delivery Approach

> [!MANDATORY]
> The delivery approach should balance speed with discipline by focusing on a carefully scoped proof of value, strong governance, and reusable foundations that can support subsequent scale without rework.

Delivery runs in four steps on one platform: Proof of Value, production pilot, chatbot rollout in department waves every 6–8 weeks, then long-list use cases. Phase durations are [NEEDS INPUT: phase durations]. Models run inside SSC-ICT's boundary, with BIO2 and Cyberbeveiligingswet controls from day one.

### 2.3 Recommended Next Steps

> [!MANDATORY]
> Following the conclusion of our engagement together, 3Point and Cisco would welcome the opportunity to engage in finalising the scope of VLAM Digital Workers and agreeing firm pricing for implementation of Phase 1. We would like to offer a series of scoping workshops to finalise the scope and support the build and roll-out of this use case, allowing SSC-ICT to move forward quickly and with minimal risk.

> [!HIGHLIGHT]
> Our recommended next step is a Proof of Value of [NEEDS INPUT: POV size in days] on a defined subset of VLAM Digital Workers: drafting and checking sampled BFF forms, TRAs and service-desk questions. ## 3. Current State and Strategic Drivers

### 3.1 Business Challenges

> [!MANDATORY]
> These challenges are typically experienced as a combination of operational strain, limited capacity, and fragmented information flows that reduce responsiveness and increase the cost of doing business.

SSC-ICT supports more than 59,000 civil servants across nine ministries. Three processes put scarce specialist time into manual document work: purchase approvals, technical risk analysis and service-desk support. Each would gain from drafting the document from existing sources and leaving the decision with a person.

**Common observations**

- Confidential and GDPR-sensitive data must not leave the organisation, so external AI services are not an option.
- External hire falls from €77.2 million in 2025 to €44.7 million in 2026, so the same work must be done with fewer contractors.

Table 1 summarises the three challenges.

| # | Challenge | Description | Urgency | Cost of Inaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Procurement lead time | Purchases above €50,000 need a long approval form. Forms that are filled in wrongly bounce back and forth for weeks. Hardware quotes stay valid for only two weeks. | Within 9 months | Missed assignments where a new quote cost tens of thousands of euros more, plus damage to reputation |
| 2 | Security specialist capacity | A technical risk analysis means a form of more than 40 pages, completed by hand from scattered sources. Security expertise is among the scarcest skills SSC-ICT needs. | Within 3 months | Audit findings, and the risk of missing relevant threats |
| 3 | Service desk at scale | The chatbot runs on hand-written rules that cover about 50% of incident types by volume. It is due to reach about 55,000 civil servants. | Within 12 months, with a new department every 6–8 weeks | A poorer user experience, extra pressure on the service desk and limited 24/7 support |

*Table 1: Business challenges*

### 3.2 Organisational Objectives

> [!MANDATORY]
> The organisational objectives identified during the engagement are best understood as a combination of improved customer experience, stronger execution discipline, and more scalable operating practices.

SSC-ICT's 2026 plan sets five strategic goals. It also commits to exploring the responsible use of AI, with transparency and explainability at its core. VLAM Digital Workers is one AI assistant, built on 3Point's 3AIgent platform for retrieval and agentic workflows. It supports four of these goals, as Table 2 shows.

| Organisational Objective | Supporting Use Case(s) | Expected Impact |

## 6. Target AI Platform

VLAM Digital Workers runs on one shared, sovereign stack: a RAG assistant that executes actions in the background, built on 3AIgent and deployed on Cisco AI PODs. 3AIgent is 3Point's retrieval and agent orchestration platform, which grounds answers in SSC-ICT's own documents and carries out workflow steps. Cisco Secure AI Factory is Cisco's validated on-premises AI infrastructure; an AI POD is its pre-sized block of compute, network and storage. Running it in SSC-ICT's government-owned data centre keeps confidential and GDPR-sensitive data inside the organisation.

> [!HIGHLIGHT]
> Cisco Secure AI Factory is SSC-ICT's enterprise AI platform, not infrastructure for one use case. All three processes run on the same secure foundation. Each added use case raises the platform's value and lowers the cost of the next, because integration, security and governance work is done once and reused.

- **Core platform:** Cisco UCS servers with NVIDIA GPUs on a Cisco Nexus fabric, with UbiOps model serving running the vLLM inference engine.
- **Integration layer:** 3AIgent connectors to VLAM, SSC-ICT's internal AI service, and to TOPdesk, Confluence, SharePoint and Exact.
- **Governance:** the VLAM gateway handles single sign-on, role-based access and audit logging.

Three principles guide the design: BIO2 and Cbw controls from day one; reuse before build; and human oversight, with security advisers keeping final responsibility for each sourced TRA draft.

### 6.1 Future Scalability

The foundation and first process come first; the other two reuse its connectors, gateway and model capacity. Each workload scales independently, so the chatbot grows with each new department without resizing other services.

## Extraction notes

- Calculation workbook R6 holds two cost bases. Inputs/PnL/AUoB/NPV keep the v0.2 draft basis (CAPEX €592,600, OPEX €838,600 a year, ROI 175%). The later TASK-017 'ROI (Section 5.1)' tab follows the newer PDF draft (one-off €442,766, 3AIgent €246,000 a year, total 5-year cost €1,672,766, net €11,489,734, ROI about 687%, payback Year 1). I used the newer Section 5.1 tab as current for costs. Benefits are identical on both bases.
- Costs on the Section 5.1 tab are the report's euro conversion of sterling figures at an implied, undated 1 GBP = 1.20 EUR. Cost lines are recorded in the original GBP: €192,072 / €230,099 / €20,595 / €246,000 equal GBP 160,060 / 191,749 / 17,163 / 205,000.
- The ROI of about 687% on the current basis is above the 3Point template 100–300% pilot guardrail. All ROIs are upper bounds, because PoV, Cisco platform, installation and SSC-ICT internal costs are excluded as [NEEDS INPUT].
- Benefits are already reduced to 60% of SSC-ICT's gross estimates (3Point conservative re-run), with Year 1 at a 50% ramp. Gross total is €4,875,000 a year; counted steady state is €2,925,000 a year; 5-year benefit is €13,162,500.
- Workbook scenarios on the v0.2 cost basis: Conservative (50%) ROI 129%, payback Year 2; Expected (60%) 175%, Year 1; Delayed start 144%, Year 2; Optimistic (100%) 358%, Year 1. NPV at 2.8% real discount rate: €7,594,646.
- Solution name: the most recent workbook tab calls it 'VLAM Digital Workers'. The older PnL/AUoB tabs call it 'AI Assistant'.
- The funnel shows 1 pilot, but no resource names which single use case is the pilot. The three selected cases (Purchase Approvals, TRA, Service Desk Chatbot) form one combined economic case on a shared architecture (3AIgent on Cisco AI Pods), and the PoV is labelled for the combined solution. All three are therefore marked 'selected'.
- Service Desk Chatbot consolidates three survey submissions (rows 3, 4 and 9). Hence 15 submitted → 13 consolidated (consolidated count marked [inferred] in the workbook).
- PoV duration: R7 (a 3Point pre-workshop dossier) plans to 'Formalize 14-day PoV charter' for whichever finalist was selected. The dossier ranked Ansible (Frame 4) top, but Ansible was later dropped. The 14 days was not adopted as the PoV size, so pov.days is null.
- No 3Point business lead or technical lead is named as such. R7 is authored by Benoit Sigwald (3Point AI), and Maarten Ectors appears in the executive readout. No customer sponsor is named as sponsor; Benjamin Clarke (MinBZK/SSC-ICT) is listed as Lead Coordinator.
- NVIDIA appears only as the GPU supplier in the Cisco stack (R7), not as a party to the engagement. UbiOps (Siebren van der Werf) and Cisco (Seda Akdemir) appear as partners in R7.
- R7 contains unverified claims (Ministry of Finance breach, Rekenkamer MTTR audit of more than 72h, '7 ministries', 'TRA from 4 weeks to <2 days'). The Annual Plan R4 states 59,000 users across nine ministries. Treat R7 figures as positioning, not facts.
- Workbook rate assumptions: blended staff rate €80/h (client-asserted, Phase 1 workshop); SSC-ICT confidence in estimates 2/5; discount rate 2.8% real; implementation year [NEEDS INPUT].
- R4 Annual Plan 2026 hooks: five strategic goals (security & compliance, execution power, innovative services, customer focus, great place to work); quotation lead time KPI >80%; scarce security/data/automation expertise named as a top-four risk; external hire cut from €77.2M (2025) to €44.7M (2026). AI is only lightly featured in the plan.

## Summary

This is a strong, well-evidenced draft written against template v1. Benefits rest on SSC-ICT's own estimates, and the conservative basis is stated openly. The appendices are unusually complete: architecture, sizing, stakeholders, KPIs and a vendor list with commercial status. The P&L arithmetic ties, and unknowns are left as `[NEEDS INPUT]` rather than invented. ## Blocking issues

### B1 — The POV is scoped and structured but has no process, size, price or recipients

- **Rule.** Section 7.1 must state the in-scope slice, a size of 20 or 40 days agreed with Phill, the commercial basis, deliverables with named recipients backed by days, and success criteria agreed in advance.
- **What is there.** The draft has in-scope and out-of-scope lists (p. 17), four receivable deliverables ending with the outcome report (p. 18) and a five-workstream effort profile (p. 18). It also has a task breakdown with acceptance criteria (pp. 37–40) and a decision gate (p. 19). Leaving the size blank rather than inventing it was correct.
- **What is missing.** The process covered (pp. 3, 9, 17, 21, 37); the size and duration (pp. 3, 9, 12, 17, 19, 21); a commercial-basis row in "POV at a glance" (p. 17); the price (p. 12); the team (pp. 17, 39); every effort figure (pp. 18, 38–39); every recipient (p. 18); and who agreed the criteria, and when (p. 19).
- **Fix.** Obtain `[NEEDS INPUT: POV process, size (20 or 40 days), elapsed weeks, team and price, agreed by Phill]` and carry the values into pp. 3, 9, 12, 17–19, 21 and 37–39. Add a "Commercial basis" row on p. 17: `[NEEDS INPUT: firm price / subject to Cisco funding discussion]`. Take the recipients from the role list on p. 41, plus `[NEEDS INPUT: names]`.

### B2 — The report says the figures are confirmed, but none of the 37 items is

- **Rule.** Every ROI figure and assumption must be confirmed by named customer staff, with dates, before the report is final.
- **What is there.** Benefits rest on SSC-ICT's own estimates, a validation session was held on 03 September 2026 (p. 31), and the 37-row register is complete (pp. 31–35).
- **The contradiction.** The text says "reviewed and confirmed as accurate by SSC-ICT staff" (p. 2), "confirmed as an accurate basis" (p. 13) and "has been reviewed… and confirmed" (p. 31). Against that, p. 31 says "Formal confirmation of each item below is the first next step", and p. 35 says "All 37 rows are awaiting confirmation". Driver 3 (57% of benefit) is back-solved with no denominator (pp. 27, 29), and SSC-ICT rates its confidence at 2 of 5 (p. 29).
- **Fix.** Keep the verbatim [!MANDATORY] text. Before the session, rebuild driver 3 from A8 × A13 × A14 (p. 29). Record `[NEEDS INPUT: name, role and date per row, from the SSC-ICT validation session]`, and set review_status to "Draft" until every row is confirmed (F7).

### B3 — The 293% ROI rests on 3Point's costs alone

- **Rule.** The investment figure must include full recurring costs and client-side effort, and the ROI is then tested against the 100–300% band.
- **What is there.** The arithmetic ties: €442,766 + 5 × €246,000 = €1,672,766, and €4,908,484 ÷ €1,672,766 = 293% (p. 12). The conservative basis is stated (p. 11), and the 687% unadjusted case is carried in the appendix (p. 30). **Missing:** the Cisco AI POD, its installation, recurring Cisco support, SSC-ICT internal effort and the POV price all sit outside the totals (pp. 11, 26, 76).
- **Fix.** Add `[NEEDS INPUT: Cisco budgetary quote via Phill; SSC-ICT internal effort]` to the P&L, then restate the headline figures on pp. 2, 12, 21 and 31.
- **Headroom against the 100% floor.** On the expected case, the ROI stays at or above 100% only while five-year cost is at most €3,290,625 (€6,581,250 ÷ 2), which allows at most €1,617,859 of added cost. On the conservative case (benefits €4,935,938), added cost can be at most €795,203. If added cost goes beyond these limits, revisit the scope, not the benefits.

### B4 — Year 1 benefits assume all three processes are live, but the roadmap phases them

- **Rule.** Payback is read off the P&L and must be consistent with the delivery plan.
- **The contradiction.** The P&L has all three drivers earning 50% in Year 1 (€731,250, p. 12), payback "under 12 months" (pp. 2, 12, 21) and a production pilot live at 6 months (p. 22). The roadmap instead runs a POV of unset length, then makes only the "POV process" live in Phase 1, with "the other two processes" following in Phase 2 (p. 19). Year 1 net is only €42,484 (p. 12), so any delay to go-live removes payback in Year 1.
- **Fix.** Time each driver from its go-live, `[NEEDS INPUT: go-live quarter per process, from the 7.2 durations]`, and read payback off the restated table. Illustration only: if Purchase Approvals alone runs at the 50% ramp in Year 1 and all three processes reach steady state in Year 2, Year 1 net = €225,000 − €688,766 = −€463,766. Payback then moves to Year 2, with cumulative net benefit of €752,734.

## Section-by-section findings

- **Section 1.** ✅ Conforms (p. 1). TOC references land on section starts, and appendix items carry no 9.X numbering and no TOC entry (pp. 1, 23).
- **Section 2.** B2 and B4 (p. 2).

## Method and limitations

- I reviewed the extracted text of all 82 PDF pages against template v1, using the measured facts as given.
- The printed-page offset is 1 (15 of 15 TOC entries agree), and all citations are printed page numbers.
- The tool did not locate section headings. I verified section starts from the page text instead: each heading appears first on its TOC page.
- The tool reported the Technical Architecture [!MANDATORY] text as "not found", but it is present on p. 48. A line-break hyphen ("user-facing") most likely defeated the match.
- I cannot see images. Apart from the header and footer logos there are none, so Figure 1 and the architecture diagrams are placeholders (pp. 15, 48), not unread artwork.
- Line spacing, space-after and the use of named styles were not measured.
- Inferred rather than verified: the B4 illustration, the 25% reduction in F2, and that the GBP rate applies to 3Point lines.
